title: A list of bytes crosses the guest boundary as one wasmtime `Val` per byte, and the lowered argument bytes are not charged to the request.
text: `convert` lowers `Value::Bytes` to a `Val::List` of `Val::U8` and lifts it back the same way (`crates/nvs-ext/src/convert.rs:194-196`, `:347-355`), because the call bridge calls every export through wasmtime's dynamic `Func::call_async`. Each byte costs a whole `Val` on the host, so a crossing costs tens of nanoseconds per byte; `benches/results/image-guest.json` shows returning decoded pixels costing about ten times the decode. The hostcall fuel is already the request's remaining memory (`crates/nvs-ext/src/call.rs:1085`, `:1259`) and running out is `Limit::Memory` (`:1241`), so a large `raw()` stops at the request's memory limit. The lifted results are charged to the request (`:961-966`), but the lowered arguments are built with no charge (`:893-907`). The decided fix: the bridge uses wasmtime's typed calls for exports whose parameters or results are `list<u8>`, one copy each way, and the lowered argument bytes are charged to the request. The `nvs:ext@1.0.0` world does not change, and third-party exports with other signatures stay on the dynamic path. `crates/nvs-ext/tests/support/image_arms.rs:23-27` sizes its frame for the per-byte cost until then.
